slides.teacher_cue: Before we begin: say the sound r — curl your tongue back without touching. This is the hardest sound for Korean learners. Mirror work begins today and continues every lesson.
slides.expected_response: Students attempt /r/ production with tongue curl before formal introduction.
slides.correction_move: Model with mirror — tongue curls back, no contact. Students copy.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution or Korean flap /ɾ/ — note any students who struggle before instruction begins.

slides.teacher_cue: Tongue tip curls back — it does not touch the roof of the mouth. Lips slightly rounded. Voice on. Hold a mirror — you should not see your tongue tip. This is the voiced post-alveolar approximant. Mirror sessions are mandatory from this lesson at every review.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /r/ with correct tongue curl and no contact with the palate.
slides.correction_move: Show contrast in mirror: /l/ — tongue tip touches ridge, contact visible. /r/ — tongue curls back, no contact. Students alternate slowly before attempting words.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution, Korean flap /ɾ/, or tongue touching the palate. Note who needs extended mirror work.

slides.teacher_cue: Say rat orally — a small rodent. Confirm /r/ production before revealing print. Blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rat orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rat orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ substitution at onset. Redirect immediately with mirror.

slides.teacher_cue: Say ran orally — past tense of run. Confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say ran orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model ran orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset and for dropping the final /n/.

slides.teacher_cue: Mime tearing paper and say rip. Confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rip orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rip orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ at onset and for the short /ɪ/ vowel quality.

slides.teacher_cue: Describe a rack as a frame for storage. Say the word, confirm /r/ onset. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say rack orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model rack orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ onset and accurate final /k/.

slides.teacher_cue: Describe a trek as a long difficult journey. Four sounds — t and r together at the start. Reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say trek orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model trek orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch whether students blend tr onset without inserting a vowel between t and r.

slides.teacher_cue: Describe a trap as a device to catch animals. Say the word, then reveal print and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say trap orally and connect meaning before print.
slides.correction_move: Model trap orally again, then reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for vowel insertion between t and r — Korean learners may produce tuh-rap.

slides.teacher_cue: Vocabulary warm-up. Say the word, connect meaning, then read it together.
slides.expected_response: Students read risk accurately.
slides.correction_move: Model the word, then repeat chorally and point to each part if needed.
slides.observation_note: Watch for smooth oral reading before it appears in connected text.
